2 2 . The revision petitioner is the accused, who suffered an order of conviction in C.C. No.104/2008,
which was confirmed in Crl.A. No.2/2015, for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 420, 465,
468 and 471 of IPC.
3.

The trial Judge passed an order of sentence as under:
"Accused is sentenced for the offence U/Sec. 409 of Indian Penal Code to undergo simple imprisonment for 3 years and sentenced to pay a five of Rs.10,000/- in default of payment of fine he shall undergo SI for 30 days.
Accused

is sentenced for the offence U/Sec. 420 of Indian Penal Code to undergo simple imprisonment for 2 years and sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- in detult of payment of fine he shall undergo SI for 30 days

Accused is sentenced for the offence U/Sec 465 of Indian Penal Code to undergo simple imprisonment for 1 year and sentenced to pay a NC: 2025:KHC-K:3776 HC-KAR fine of Rs.1,000/- in default of payment of fine he shall undergo SI for 15 days.

Accused is sentenced for the offence U/Sec. 468 of Indian Penal Code to undergo simple imprisonment for 2 years and sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- in default of payment of fine he shall undergo SI for 15 days

Accused is sentenced for the offence U/Sec. 471 of Indian Penal Code to undergo simple imprisonment for 1 year and sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- in default of payment of fine he shall undergo SI for 15 days Bail bonds of the accused and his surety bond shall stand cancelled."

4. The same was challenged before the First Appellate Court in Crl.A. No.2/2015 and learned Judge in the First Appellate Court after securing the records heard the arguments of the parties in detail and by considered judgment dated 12.10.2020 dismissed the appeal of the accused and confirmed the order of the Trial Judge.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:3776 HC-KAR 5. Being further aggrieved by the same, accused is before this Court in this revision.

6. Facts as could be seen from the records of the Trial Court shows that a complaint came to be lodged by the Manager of the Krishna Grameen Bank, Jewargi Branch, alleging the misappropriation of the amount by the accused, who was Accountant in the said branch.

He remained absent between 08.06.2004 and 21.07.2004 and thereafter, there were sixteen withdrawals, by forging documents causing loss to the extent of Rs.3,50,000/-.
7.
After thorough investigation, police filed charge- sheet and after due trial, accused was convicted for the aforesaid offences.

sentences.text: The validity of the order of conviction was challenged before the First Appellate Court by the accused.

9. Learned Judge in the First Appellate Court after re-appreciation of the material evidence, took note of fact that the case of the prosecution predominantly hinged on NC: 2025:KHC-K:3776 HC-KAR the documentary evidence rather than the oral evidence of the parties.

10. Admittedly, sixteen withdrawal slips which were forged by the accused have been sent to the Experts and noted that forgery has taken place and an amount of Rs.3,50,000/- was withdrawn by the accused, thus, it is clear case of misappropriation under Section 409 of IPC.

11. Accused being the Accountant, there was an automatic entrustment of the documents and the cash with the accused therefore, he is liable for the alleged offences under Sections 409, 420, 465,
468 and 471 of IPC.

12. When two Courts have categorically recorded an order of conviction, in the absence of any plausible explanation offered by the accused while recording the accused statement, mere denial of the incriminatory circumstances would not be sufficient for this Court to annul the order of conviction.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:3776 HC-KAR 13.
Taking note of these aspects of the matter, this Court is of the considered opinion that the order of conviction needs to be maintained.
14. Having said thus, accused is now aged 69 years and he is suffering from old age ailments and being the first time offender,

if the sentence of imprisonment ordered by the Trial Magistrate is modified by directing the accused to undergo simple imprisonment for a day and also directing him to pay a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as the enhanced fine amount taking note of the fact that the misappropriated amount of Rs.3,50,000/- is already recovered from the accused, ends of justice would be met.

15. Accordingly, following order is passed:
ORDER a) Revision petition is allowed in part.

b) While maintaining the order of conviction of the revision petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 420, 465, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, NC: 2025:KHC-K:3776 HC-KAR sentence of imprisonment ordered by the Trial Magistrate confirmed by the First Appellate Court is modified by directing the accused/revision petitioner to undergo simple imprisonment for a day till rising of the Court and to pay enhanced fine amount of Rs.1,00,000/- on before 31.07.2025.
Ramappa S/O Yallappa Waddar vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10066761/
4 c) Failure to pay the enhanced fine amount of Rs.1,00,000/- on or before 31.07.2025, the order of sentence passed by the Trial Magistrate confirmed by the First Appellate Court stands restored automatically.
 d) Out of the fine amount, a sum of  Rs.75,000/- is ordered to be paid as compensation to Krishna Grameena Bank, Jewargi under due identification.
e) Office is directed to return the Trial Court records with copy of this order forthwith for issue of modified conviction warrant.
Sd/-
(V. SRISHANANDA) JUDGE SBS,SRT CT:PK Ramappa S/O Yallappa Waddar vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10066761/
